tldr: Claude Fable 5 launched as Anthropic's flagship model, with Claude Opus 5 arriving alongside it as a cheaper tier matching Fable-level benchmarks at roughly half the price. That pricing frame set the stage for the model's first independent hands-on test.
whats_new: Simon Willison one-shotted a playable Raccoon Heist browser game with Claude Fable 5, redoing a GPT-3/DALL-E game-concept test he first tried four years ago.
why_it_matters: A working one-shot game from a single prompt is an early, informal read on Fable 5's agentic code-generation ceiling ahead of formal coding-agent benchmarks.

beats.headline: Opus 5 launches as the cheaper option, matching Fable 5 on benchmarks
beats.summary: Opus 5 hits Fable-level performance at roughly half Fable's price, reported across four outlets.

beats.headline: Builder one-shots a playable game with Fable 5
beats.summary: Simon Willison generates a complete Raccoon Heist game from a single prompt, four years after running the same test on GPT-3 and DALL-E.

open_questions: Does Fable 5's one-shot coding performance hold up on multi-file builds beyond a single browser game?
Do independent evals confirm Opus 5 matches Fable 5's performance at half the price, or is that Anthropic's own framing?
take_for_builders: Run Fable 5 against your own coding-agent eval suite before assuming parity with Opus 5's lower price point — the one-shot game demo is illustrative, not a benchmark.

day_captions.c34a327604b5be4a: Establishes Fable 5 as the flagship price/performance reference point Opus 5 undercuts.
day_captions.9cfe688a300dc5e4: First independent hands-on build showing Fable 5's one-shot coding capability.
